News.title: Moment Delta flight bursts into flames in explosion seconds after take-off
News.content:
A packed plane burst into flames following an explosion seconds after take-off.

The drama occurred just before midnight yesterday at Sao Paulo’s Guarulhos International Airport, the largest airport in Brazil and Latin America, causing a fire next to the runway which emergency responders had to rush to put out.

Video footage of the take-off and subsequent blast shows the scorched material from the packed plane falling to the ground and setting light to grass. The pilot of the Delta Air Lines Airbus A330-323 declared ‘Mayday’ before making an emergency landing.

The plane was on its way to Atlanta in the United States, with the flight lasting just over nine minutes. Nearly 300 passengers were reportedly on board the jet, which stopped its climb at 4,500ft to return to the terminal.

An air traffic controller, in a conversation with the flight commander, said: “Delta, you have fire on your wings” and the pilot responded: “We know, we will need to return.”

There were no reports of any injuries. Delta Air Lines said on its website it had cancelled flight DL0104 due to mechanic problems and apologised for the inconvenience.

It comes as a major European country has closed its airspace to US warplanes involved in the conflict with Iran.

Image: SBGR LIVE/Youtube) SBGR LIVE/Youtube)

US planes involved in the war will not be allowed to land at bases in Spain or use its airspace. Donald Trump has already been angered by Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez over his lack of support for the war effort.

Since the start of the war, Spain has not allowed fighter jets or other US warplanes to use the Rota (Cádiz) and Morón de la Frontera (Seville) airbases. The Spanish leader has been Europe’s most consistently vocal critic of Trump, who threatened "to cut off all trade" with the country earlier this month for not allowing the US to use military bases.

The spat intensified when Spain’s foreign minister contradicted a claim by the White House press secretary that Spain had heard Trump’s message “loud and clear” and was cooperating with the US military. While denouncing the repressive government in Tehran, Sánchez said he would not back a war that he said was an unjustified assault.

News.title: Beatrice, Eugenie and Fergie's nickname showed their closeness – now they're 'cast adrift'
News.content:
Beatrice, Eugenie and Fergie's nickname showed their closeness – now they're 'cast adrift'

Princess Beatrice and Princess Eugenie once shared a nickname with their mother Sarah Ferguson, but sources say the royal sisters are now deeply disappointed with Fergie following the Andrew scandal

View 5 Images Beatrice, Sarah and Eugenie called themselves 'The Tripod' (Image: Getty)

Not so long ago, Princess Eugenie, Princess Beatrice and Sarah Ferguson coined a private nickname to mark their special bond. But times have changed dramatically.

‌



In the aftermath of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's very public fall from grace, his ex-wife and two daughters find themselves navigating completely unfamiliar territory. Since Andrew was stripped of his titles and honours in October last year, Sarah, Beatrice and Eugenie have each adopted strikingly different ways of handling the situation.

‌



Eugenie, who is based in Portugal, has reportedly been trying to distance herself from her disgraced father, while Beatrice appears to be standing more firmly by his side. Their mother, meanwhile, has vanished from public life entirely, with speculation that she had been laying low at the home of close friend Priscilla Presley being quashed over the weekend.

‌



It's a world away from the golden era of "The Tripod," as royal expert Emily Nash highlights on this week's Hello! Magazine podcast. Reflecting on their closeness in a 2008 interview with The Telegraph, Eugenie said: "Mummy, Bea and I call ourselves 'The Tripod'. They are my best friends in the world."

Emily explains: "They now find themselves on the edge and slightly cast adrift from the rest of the Royal Family because everyone's waiting to see what else might come out of the woodwork."

View 5 Images Although none of the allegations have been proven, Andrew's arrest changed everything (Image: Getty)

‌



A family friend has told the Daily Mail's royal editor Rebecca English that Beatrice and Eugenie are both deeply disappointed in their mother. "Beatrice and Eugenie are lovely girls and they have been left bereft by this all," the source said. "I would actually go so far as to say that they are even more disappointed in their mother than their father now.

"The tripod has collapsed. Obviously they will continue to support their parents, but they feel so let down."

The three members of "The Tripod" have not been pictured together in recent months. Sarah Ferguson's current whereabouts remain unknown. According to a recent Page Six report, the King's former sister-in-law is "effectively homeless" after both daughters reportedly refused to accommodate her in the homes they share with their respective husbands and children.

‌



View 5 Images The three were once inseparable (Image: Getty)

Up until February this year, Sarah had resided in a wing of her ex-husband's grand residence - Royal Lodge on the Windsor Home Park estate. She had proudly claimed that despite their 1996 divorce, she and Andrew remained extremely close, saying: "We're the happiest divorced couple in the world. We're divorced to each other, not from each other."

In Entitled, Andrew Lownie's explosive biography of Andrew and Sarah, the former prince is quoted as even musing about rekindling their marriage. "I don't rule remarriage out and I certainly don't rule it in," Andrew reportedly said, adding: "If ever the opportunity arose, I do not know what I would do, as it is not in the plan."

‌



While friends privately revealed that Sarah had no wish to "put her head back into that lion's cage", she publicly declared her unwavering loyalty to him, telling the Daily Mail: "My duty is to him. I am so proud of him. I stand by him and always will."

But following the loss of Royal Lodge's tenancy, Sarah has not been publicly spotted with her former husband.

View 5 Images Andrew's freindship with Jeffrey Epstein has cast a shadow over his family (Image: Getty)

‌



Commenting on their relationship to the Mail, royal commentator Richard Fitzwilliams said: "The world can clearly see that the previous arrangement was designed to maximise the benefit of Andrew's public life for them privately.

"The procession of dubious friends including an alleged Chinese spy over many years spoke for itself. The public have been appalled by them, the politicians are restive and there is almost certainly much more to come in the Epstein files."

He further noted that securing a suitable residence for Andrew had proved particularly troublesome, despite the considerable extent of the Royal Family's estates: "The problem is that the Waleses will not want them as neighbours - who would? If there's one thing that William and Kate won't want, it is Andrew and Fergie in close proximity."

‌



Beatrice and Eugenie have similarly maintained a low profile, while numerous questions have been raised regarding the royal sisters' prospects. There has been conjecture that they could also face the loss of their royal titles. With the inquiry into Mountbatten-Windsor continuing, the royal sisters find themselves in uncertainty as potentially life-altering decisions hang over their unclear futures.

View 5 Images Sarah and Andrew were both turfed out of Royal Lodge in February (Image: Getty)

Both Beatrice and Eugenie were additionally mentioned in documents disclosed from the FBI inquiry into Jeffrey Epstein.

Article continues below

One of the published emails appears to indicate that Sarah brought Beatrice and Eugenie, then aged 20 and 19, to "celebrate" Epstein's prison release in 2009. Neither princess has yet addressed any of these allegations.

While the inclusion of their names in the files does not itself indicate any misconduct, demands have grown for the princesses to discuss what they might know about their parents' connection with the late convicted sex offender.

Royal commentator Jennie Bond told the Mirror: "I've said before and I repeat that I think it would be best for both Beatrice and Eugenie give up their royal titles and live an entirely private life. So far they have not chosen to do so. Nor have they given their account of what they knew about Epstein and their parents' friendship with him."

News.title: Nanny's harrowing final days tortured and starved to death in living nightmare
News.content:
Nanny's harrowing final days tortured and starved to death in living nightmare

Sophie Lionnet thought she had found the perfect family to work for, but things quickly unravelled as her cruel and brutal bosses subjected her to a campaign of terrible abuse

View 4 Images Sophie had moved to the UK to live with the couple (Image: PA)

Sophie Lionnet thought she had found the perfect family to work for when she left her hometown of Troyes in north-east France and moved to London to start as an au-pair.

‌



The bright and bubbly 21-year-old wanted to improve her English and experience life in the UK, and to live in a million pound home in leafy Wimbledon with fashion designer Sabrina Kouider and her partner Ouissem Medouni seemed like an opportunity that was too good to miss.

‌



Instead, it became a living nightmare that would result in her death.

‌



Behind the doors of their home on Wimbledon Park Road, Sophie was starved, interrogated and tortured over months of escalating paranoia. A heartbreaking note later found after her death read: “Why me? I need help to stop them.”

View 4 Images It's unknown exactly how she died (Image: Facebook )

Kouider, 35, had become consumed by a delusional obsession with her former boyfriend, Mark Walton, who is a founding member of the band Boyzone.

‌



She convinced herself that Sophie was having an affair with him and had helped her ex devise plot against her. There was no evidence for any of it, with Walton eventually telling the Old Bailey he had never even met the young nanny.

Prosecutors said Kouider and her husband Medouni subjected Sophie to “pressure and relentless intimidation”, recording hours of footage in which a terrified Sophie was accused of being a spy, a paedophile and part of some elaborate conspiracy.

They even threatened the french national with rape, imprisonment and further violence if she did not confess.

‌



View 4 Images Sabrina Kouider (L) and her partner Ouissem Medouni (R),were found guilty of murdering their old au-pair, Sophie Lionnet (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

Over time, the interrogations would turn violent.. Sophie was beaten and whipped with a cable, a barage of abuse which left her with fractures to her sternum, four ribs and her jawbone.

In the days before she died she was even deprived of food, becoming visibly thinner in the videos the couple filmed.

‌



Tragically, warning signs of abuse were missed. A local restaurant owner said Sophie once told him that Kouider had beaten her up because she had “dropped the butter.”

Despite sensing something was wrong, he admitted he had no idea the scale of the abuse.

Sophie had even written to her family saying she wanted to leave. Investigators later discovered her passport and a plane ticket home were missing.

‌



View 4 Images The haunting final photo of Sophie (Image: PA)

While we know Sophie was killed at the hands of Koudier and Medouni, we don't know exactly how she was murdered due to damage suffered to her body post-mortem.

In an attempt to destroy the evidence, Kouider and Medouni set about burning Sophie’s body using their garden barbecue.

Article continues below

When firefighters arrived after neighbours reported a foul smell, one spotted what looked like nose and fingers among the remains. Medouni claimed it was the carcass of a sheep, although didn't fool anybody.

The jury rejected the couple’s attempts to blame each other. They were convicted of murder and jailed for life, each ordered to serve a minimum of 30 years.

Speaking after the verdict, Sophie’s aunt described her as “a pearl. Kind, gentle. She loved everyone.”

News.title: 'I'm a security expert and you must do two things with your body if nuclear strike hits UK'
News.content:
'I'm a security expert and you must do two things with your body if nuclear strike hits UK'

UK government issues nuclear attack survival advice as historian warns Britain is 'not prepared' for threats from Iran - and Downing Street finalises new defence plan

View 3 Images The first 24 hours is the most important (Image: Getty)

Downing Street has released guidance on how to protect your body in the critical moments following a nuclear attack as the government puts the finishing touches to its defence strategy.

‌



Iran possesses missiles with the range to strike the UK, and military historian and author Dr Mark Felton has weighed in on Iran's ballistic capabilities.

‌



Speaking to his YouTube subscribers on Mark Felton Productions, Felton said the UK is "not prepared for any such attacks".

‌



He stressed Britain lacks an Israeli-style Iron Dome defence network or surface-to-air missile systems protecting our critical infrastructure or atomic facilities.

The initial action you must take is simply to avert your gaze, reports the Express.

View 3 Images This is what to do if bombs fall (Image: Getty)

‌



The blinding flash produced by a nuclear detonation and the subsequent orange fireball can inflict permanent harm to your vision, according to Business Insider.

A 1-megaton device, 80 times more powerful than the atomic weapon unleashed on Hiroshima in 1945, could temporarily blind individuals up to 13 miles away on a bright day.

This distance extends to 53 miles away during a clear night, as documented by Atomic Archive.

‌



Your next move should be to throw yourself to the ground as swiftly as possible, face downwards, following official guidance from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Subsequently, tuck your hands beneath your body for protection against burns, debris and flames.

View 3 Images The first thing you need to do is avert your eyes (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Should you have something to cover your nose and mouth, use it, and ensure your mouth remains open to prevent your eardrums from rupturing due to pressure changes.

Sir Keir Starmer indicated the Defence Investment Plan was approaching final sign-off and sat on his desk in Downing Street.

When questioned whether this was accurate while appearing before the Liaison Committee of senior MPs, the Prime Minister responded: "Yes, and... we are finalising it. But I'm absolutely determined that I will make commitments with appropriate funding that I can be sure is there. I will not make commitments without being clear where the funding is coming from.

‌



"That is what has gone on for years, and that's why we are in the mess that we're in."

Sir Keir engaged in a heated exchange with Sir Bernard Jenkin, a Conservative committee member who argued the Government displayed a "lack of war fighting mentality" and alleged defence decision-making "smacks of enormous complacency".

The Prime Minister fired back: "Well this smacks of the fact that for years there was under investment by the last government and the 'hollowing out of our armed forces', copyright Ben Wallace."

Article continues below

Conservative former defence secretary Sir Ben previously argued whilst serving in government that the armed forces had been "hollowed out and underfunded".

News.title: BBC expert's advice for people taking ibuprofen, naproxen, diclofenac
News.content:
BBC expert's advice for people taking ibuprofen, naproxen, diclofenac

Dr Punam Krishan appeared on BBC Morning Live after Kidney Care UK and the National Pharmacy Association issued a warning about some painkillers

View Image Dr Punam Krishan spoke out about painkillers on BBC Morning Live amid concerns (Image: BBC)

A BBC specialist has issued fresh guidance following warnings about medications taken by millions across Britain. Kidney Care UK and the National Pharmacy Association (NPA) released an alert earlier this month concerning anyone taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) such as ibuprofen, naproxen, and diclofenac.

‌



Specialists warned that those at greater risk of kidney disease, including people with diabetes or high blood pressure, ought to exercise particular caution, as these medications can raise blood pressure and harm blood vessels in the kidneys. Speaking on BBC Morning Live, Dr Punam Krishan emphasised that patients taking these types of painkillers 'long term' must maintain regular consultations with their GP.

‌



Dr Punam said: "So many people use painkillers. Some people might be using it for a period of time for an acute problem or be on them long term. And sometimes I think there can be bit of stigma attached to being on painkillers. Now look at there's different types of painkillers. You've got paracetamol, you've got non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. So examples of that are ibuprofen, naproxen, diclofenac, you've got your opioids. So that's codeine or tramadol morphine based medications. And then you've got painkillers that help with nerve pain.

‌



"Some people might be on one, some people might be on a combination of these. Now when you look at headlines like this, it suggests that painkillers in general cause kidney damage and that's not the case. They're referring to non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs in this headline and this isn't new. So, we know that these medications work by blocking inflammation.

"What they can do though by doing that they can reduce blood flow to the kidneys and in some people they can increase blood pressure if you've got pre-existing kidney issues. Now, in general, if you're fit and well, you've got no other kidney problems, taking anti-inflammatory medications is absolutely fine. If you are on them long term, your GP have a handle on it. It's why we do general reviews with people that are on repeat painkillers."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



She urged those who had been prescribed the medication not to abandon their course of treatment out of worry, and instead seek advice from their GP. She explained: "People can sometimes just suddenly stop taking their painkillers. And the thing is they serve a purpose. Of course, you shouldn't take something if you don't need it.

"But if you're just kind of carrying on without painkillers and trying to soldier your own, actually it affects your quality of life and other aspects of your life. So, it's just making sure that you're checking in with your doctor if you're regularly on them. If you are taking them over the counter and you don't know what the root cause of the pain is, see your GP so we can investigate that."

Speaking about the warning issued earlier this month, Olivier Picard, chair of the NPA, stated: "Medicines have the power to harm as well as to heal. "Although NSAIDs, such as ibuprofen, are effective and safe medicines, patients should be aware of their impact - particularly if a patient is at increased risk of developing kidney disease - and consider alternative medication where appropriate.

‌



"If a patient has concerns about their usage of NSAIDs, they should speak to their pharmacist who can advise them. Pharmacists are experts in medicines and are best placed to offer advice to people who may be concerned about any potential long-term effect of some medicines and can help patients effectively manage pain."

Approximately 7.2 million people across the UK are currently living with some form of chronic kidney disease, which typically presents no symptoms during its early stages. Kidney Care UK also suggests that roughly one million individuals remain undiagnosed. Those at heightened risk of developing the condition include: people with diabetes; individuals with high blood pressure; those with a family history of kidney disease; and people from black and south Asian backgrounds.

Fiona Loud, policy director at Kidney Care UK, said: "Kidney disease can happen to anyone at any time, and can have a devastating impact on your life, relationships, finances as well as your physical and mental health."

Article continues below

Among the 294,999 individuals who used the charity's kidney health checker between October 2024 and March 2026, nearly a quarter (24%) reported regularly taking over-the-counter painkillers.
